Sasha: heads up — pass@k numbers on the new runner look inflated after int8 quant experiments. saw 0.72 -> 0.95 on duplicates.
Olivia: whoa, can you paste the runner logs? link to CI job? :eyes:
Sasha: https://ci.internal/jobs/1234 — failed run. Here's excerpt:
```
PASS_AT_K: 0.95
sampled=100 deduped=80 hits=95
```
Eval-bot: nightly/eval-runner #1234 failed: metric_mismatch threshold exceeded
Sanjay: could be sampling/dedupe order + float->int cast in `pass_at_k` calc. If denominator uses unique candidates vs sampled k it inflates.
Maria: quick check of our impl:
```
def pass_at_k(preds, refs, k):
    hits = 0
    for p_list, r in zip(preds, refs):
        topk = p_list[:k]
        if any(normalize(x) == normalize(r) for x in topk):
            hits += 1
    return hits / len(preds)
```
Olivia: that looks fine but `p_list` sometimes is a flat string from quantized runner (weird). tokenization differences (fast-bpe vs hf tokenizer) also affect BERTScore variance.
Sasha: repro steps: `pytest tests/evals/test_passatk.py::test_quantized_model --seed=42` failing only with int8 on CUDA, not fp16 on same samples.
Sanjay: theory: quantized model returns deterministic but differently-batched candidate ordering; if we dedupe after slicing top-k we can double-count. add explicit dedupe+sort before slicing. also ensure k cast: `k = int(k)`
Maria: I'll open a small PR: normalizes candidates, dedupe then sort by model score, then slice. add explicit `k = max(1, int(k))`. will add CI smoke test for quantized runner.
Sasha: also seeing BERTScore delta ~0.03 after tokenization change in our tokenizer migration. need parity tests in CI for BERTScore tokenization.
Eval-bot: created ticket INF-482: add pass@k parity tests and tokenization checks
Olivia: nice. can we add a blurb in onboarding docs about metric caveats with quantization and tokenizer mismatches? short note in /docs/evals/metrics.md
Sasha: will draft and link the PR to INF-482. thanks all :thumbsup:
